note: Source of truth for delivery and compliance status. One item per line: diffs read as one line per requirement. Regenerate views with `python3 tools/progress/progress.py build` after every edit.

items.title: The deciding unit is the household, not the child
items.summary: Career choice is a family portfolio decision; social evaluation is a real utility term. A tool that only talks to the teenager gets overridden at the dinner table.
items.implication: The core deliverable is a negotiation artifact for the family (M3); the parent is a first-class user (R-2).

items.title: Occupational awareness is narrow, and Soviet-inflected at the parent level
items.summary: An interest inventory administered over unfamiliar occupations measures familiarity and prestige, not interest.
items.implication: Exposure (M1) precedes and feeds assessment (M2); exposure history is a first-class data stream.

items.title: Self-report psychometrics degrade in predictable ways
items.summary: Acquiescence bias, social desirability, unfamiliar Likert conventions, the instinct that every test has a correct answer, and a parent beside the child on a shared phone.
items.implication: Format-level countermeasures, not translation-level ones. No 'test' language, no visible score.

items.title: The prestige economy and the wage economy have diverged, and lock-in comes early
items.summary: Medicine and law are oversubscribed relative to returns; subject-block choice around grades 9-10 forecloses paths before discovery normally happens.
items.implication: Primary audience grades 7-9; every recommendation carries a financing path and a subject-block plan; vocational routes get production parity.

items.title: Constraints are structured by gender and geography
items.summary: Some families cap a daughter's options by marriage timing; some professions are socially coded; mobility to Tashkent is a live constraint for regional children.
items.implication: Constraints enter only as explicit family-stated inputs, never as platform-encoded rules. The possibility space is expanded through content.

items.title: Infrastructure realities
items.summary: Telegram is the distribution layer; cheap shared Android devices; thin regional bandwidth; two Uzbek scripts plus Russian; in-country hosting required; users are minors.
items.implication: Mini App primary with full web parity; single-source content with transliteration; low-bandwidth defaults; residency, consent and shared-device safety are architectural.

items.title: The state has already created our category
items.summary: The September 2025 decree on mandatory school advisors turned a vague obligation into a named, staffed, under-tooled role.
items.implication: The B2B pitch is the advisor's operating system, not extra work. Private schools are the beachhead.

items.title: Exposure before assessment
items.summary: The explorer feeds the instrument.
items.violation_test: Any interest item referencing an occupation the child has not been shown, or any child-facing item using bare occupation names.

items.title: Behavior over self-description
items.summary: Choices, task performance and usage traces outrank agree/disagree statements.
items.violation_test: Likert agree-scales appearing in the child flow; a release where telemetry-derived signals are not part of the profile.

items.title: The family is the user
items.summary: Three-sided product - child, parent, advisor - and the flagship output is a structured family conversation.
items.violation_test: A launch plan or report design in which the parent has no role, or in which the child's result is framed as a verdict to be delivered to the parent.

items.title: Pathways, not labels
items.summary: Output is always plural, provisional and concrete: next subject block, next course, next cost, plan B.
items.violation_test: Any UI surface showing a type label, a single recommendation, or a score; fewer than three pathways in any generated report.

items.title: Local validity is built, not imported
items.summary: RIASEC is the starting hypothesis; every item is instrumented; the interest structure is re-derived from Uzbek data.
items.violation_test: Shipping item changes without telemetry; treating the Holland hexagon as settled truth in scoring code; hard-coding weights no one can trace to data.

items.title: Student
items.summary: Grades 7-9 primary, 10-11 secondary. Uses explorer, assessment, pathway planner.

items.title: Parent / guardian
items.summary: Runs the parallel parent instrument, receives the family congruence report, holds consent.

items.title: Family broker (optional)
items.summary: The relative whose opinion actually carries. Invited as a viewer of the family report.

items.title: School advisor
items.summary: The decree-mandated role and primary B2B user: aggregates, one-at-a-time summaries, report generation, parent-meeting log.

items.title: School administrator / director
items.summary: The buyer. Sees aggregate analytics only.

items.title: Content editor (internal)
items.summary: Maintains career cards, pathway templates, media, translations and verification dates.

items.title: Research lead (internal)
items.summary: Owns the item bank, telemetry analysis, norms and validation studies.

items.title: Occupation Explorer
items.summary: The content engine and the moat: builds occupational awareness, supplies the assessment's item pool, logs exposure.

items.title: Assessment Suite
items.summary: Produces a student profile from behavior and structured choice rather than self-description.

items.title: Family Module
items.summary: Converts the child's profile and the parents' aspirations into a structured negotiation, not a confrontation.

items.title: Pathway Planner
items.summary: Turns profiles and constraints into named, financed, plural routes.

items.title: School Layer
items.summary: The advisor's operating system, including the reporting the role already owes.

items.title: Research Layer
items.summary: Turns usage into validity: item statistics, local norms, and the evidence base Phase 3 requires.

items.title: Mentorship (deferred by design)
items.summary: Async Q&A first, then group formats. The only MVP-era dependency is that career cards can host threaded content later.
items.note: Elaborated in the mentorship concept document; MP/MS/T/ME items below are not yet binding.

items.title: Career card model
items.summary: Every card carries titles and body in uz-Latn/uz-Cyrl/ru, cluster tags, daily reality, entry routes, subject-block mapping, cost band, regional wage ranges at years 1/5/10, geography of demand, related cards, media refs, sources[] and last_verified.

items.title: Video content
items.summary: 60-90 second 'bir kun' day-in-the-life videos with real people; every video has a low-bandwidth variant (audio + stills).

items.title: Exposure logging
items.summary: Every card view logs dwell time, replays, returns and completion; this stream gates M2 scoring eligibility and feeds M6.

items.title: Browse and search
items.summary: Browse and search by cluster, tag and free text, in all three locales and both scripts.

items.title: Content policy (enforced at review)
items.summary: Deliberate over-indexing on regional role models, women in nontraditional fields shown matter-of-factly, dignified skilled-trade arcs. No gender-coded card copy.

items.title: Item formats
items.summary: Forced-choice triads over illustrated activities, situational-judgment items in local scenes, performance mini-tasks with timing, an 8-card values sort, and constraints intake.

items.title: Exposure rule
items.summary: Interest items reference only activities or occupations already surfaced via M1. Bare occupation names are forbidden in the child flow.

items.title: Session engine
items.summary: 10-15 minute resumable chunks with server-side state; a full profile accumulates across sessions. Designed for shared devices and 45-minute lessons.

items.title: Scoring v1
items.summary: Internal vectors only - interest, values, aptitude, constraints. Scoring must be traceable to item data; weights are configuration, not constants buried in code.

items.title: Child-facing output
items.summary: Playful, non-evaluative feedback plus unlocked pathway suggestions. No scores, no types, no pass/fail.

items.title: Constraints intake
items.summary: Explicit family-context questions - budget band, mobility, non-negotiables - stored as stated constraints and used by M4. Never inferred.

items.title: Parent instrument
items.summary: About 10 minutes: aspiration picks, non-negotiables, an occupational-map exercise surfacing outdated assumptions gently, and flexibility items.

items.title: Invitation flow
items.summary: Child or advisor invites the parent by Telegram deep link; parent onboarding completes in one sitting on a low-end phone.

items.title: Family congruence report
items.summary: Where child profile and parent aspirations overlap, where they diverge (framed neutrally), three concrete pathways inside the overlap, and a conversation guide.

items.title: Third seat
items.summary: Optional invited viewer for the family broker who actually moves the decision.

items.title: Hard privacy rules
items.summary: Parents see fit and options, never the child's item-level answers. All child-visible output must be safe if seen by a parent on a shared device.

items.title: Pathway template model
items.summary: Target occupations, education step, subject block and exam requirements, cost band, financing options, timeline, plausible first job, plan-B link, region variants, surface flags.

items.title: Matching engine v1
items.summary: Rules and template matching over profile x constraints. No ML in MVP; every match must be explainable in one sentence.

items.title: Plurality rule
items.summary: Every generated plan contains at least three routes, always including at least one non-university route where constraints allow.

items.title: Surface flags
items.summary: Migration-related pathway content renders on the consumer surface only; the school-facing surface receives the softened variant.

items.title: Rostering
items.summary: Class codes; no school-side IT integration required in Phase 2.

items.title: Advisor dashboard
items.summary: Class-level aggregate heatmaps, no-signal flags for profiles needing a human conversation, one-at-a-time student summaries with access logging.

items.title: Report generator
items.summary: One-click generation of the career-orientation documentation the advisor role requires, from aggregates. Templates are content-configurable, not hard-coded.

items.title: Parent-meeting log
items.summary: Tied to family reports, with the family's consent.

items.title: Lab mode
items.summary: Batch student sessions on shared lab machines: low bandwidth, resumable, queue-and-sync tolerant of connectivity drops.

items.title: Explicit non-features
items.summary: No ranked lists, no individual score exports, no class-results spreadsheet. Refused at the product level, permanently.
items.violation_test: Any endpoint, export, or dashboard view that returns students ordered by any score-derived value.

items.title: Telemetry schema
items.summary: Exposure events, item responses with latency, session events - versioned, and present from the first pilot build.

items.title: Item bank and statistics pipeline
items.summary: Per-item statistics: usage balance for forced-choice, discrimination, latency flags, comprehension flags.

items.title: Norms jobs
items.summary: Norms by cohort, region, and language/script of administration.

items.title: Structure analysis readiness
items.summary: Export shapes suitable for testing whether the six-factor interest structure holds locally, with re-clustering as the expected outcome rather than a failure.

items.title: Follow-up scheduler
items.summary: 6- and 18-month follow-ups via Telegram (choice made, satisfaction, persistence) - the criterion-validation loop.

items.title: De-identified research exports
items.summary: Research exports are de-identified only.

items.title: Device floor
items.summary: Fully usable on Android 8 / 2 GB RAM class devices inside the Telegram webview, and in low-end desktop browsers for lab mode.
items.verification: Device-matrix pass on three low-end Android devices plus one iOS Telegram client.

items.title: Payload budget
items.summary: Mini App core interactive bundle at or under ~300 KB gzipped; media lazy-loaded; usable on a ~500 kbps connection.
items.verification: Bundle-size budget check in CI once a stack exists.

items.title: Performance
items.summary: p95 API latency under 500 ms in-country; assessment interactions render feedback in under 100 ms locally.

items.title: Availability
items.summary: At least 99.5% in Phase 1, with degraded-mode reads of cached explorer content when the API is unreachable.
items.verification: Uptime monitoring plus an offline-read test.

items.title: Locale parity
items.summary: 100% of UI strings in uz-Latn, uz-Cyrl and ru at every release, with per-script rendered-screenshot QA.
items.verification: Locale-completeness check in CI plus screenshot review per release.

items.title: Resumability
items.summary: Any session chunk survives connection loss and device handoff without data loss.
items.verification: Throttled and drop-injection tests on the assessment flow.

items.title: Accessibility and literacy
items.summary: Adjustable text size, icon-supported navigation, reading level calibrated in Phase 0 for grade 7.
items.verification: Reading-level calibration during the Phase-0 pilot.

items.title: Auditability
items.summary: Every advisor access to individual data is logged and reviewable.
items.verification: Audit-log integration test on advisor read paths.

items.title: Plural, provisional outputs
items.summary: Every report contains at least three pathways with explicitly provisional framing. No single verdicts, ever.
items.violation_test: A generated report with fewer than three pathways, or output phrased as a settled recommendation.

items.title: No type labels
items.summary: RIASEC and successor structures are internal vocabulary only; no type labels in child- or parent-facing UI.
items.violation_test: Any RIASEC letter, code, or type name reachable from a child or parent surface.

items.title: No ranked lists or individual score exports
items.summary: A product-level refusal designed to precede institutional requests for it. Advisor access to individuals is one-at-a-time and logged.
items.violation_test: Any ordering of students by a score-derived value, or any export containing individual scores.

items.title: Parents see congruence and options, never item-level answers
items.summary: The parent view is derived, never raw.
items.violation_test: Any parent-reachable response containing per-item child responses.

items.title: No gender- or region-conditional logic
items.summary: Constraints enter scoring and matching only as explicit family-stated inputs.
items.violation_test: Any branch in scoring or matching code keyed on gender or region rather than on a stated constraint.

items.title: Shared-device safety
items.summary: Every child-visible screen must be safe if seen by a parent.
items.violation_test: A child-facing screen whose disclosure to a parent would harm the child.

items.title: Low-stakes framing
items.summary: No scores, no pass/fail, game language not exam language. Both an ethics rule and the anti-gaming strategy.
items.violation_test: The word 'test'/'imtihon' or any visible score in the child flow.

items.title: Consent and data rights
items.summary: Parental consent plus child assent, deletion on request, de-identified research exports, aggregate-only publication.
items.violation_test: Any data collection before a recorded consent, or an export carrying identifiers.

items.title: Migration content surface rule
items.summary: Migration content appears on the consumer surface only; the school surface carries the softened variant.
items.violation_test: Migration-flagged content rendered on a school-facing surface.

items.title: Vocational dignity parity
items.summary: Trades and certificate routes get the same content production value and matching weight as university routes.
items.violation_test: A content batch or matching weight set in which vocational routes are systematically thinner.

items.title: Broker provisioning
items.summary: The module's core purpose is supplying broker-poor families with a credible third voice; family-facing formats are the point, not an add-on.
items.violation_test: A roadmap in which family-visible formats trail child-only formats indefinitely.

items.title: Biographical matching
items.summary: Students are routed to mentors by pathway interest plus biographical proximity, never by assessment profile.
items.violation_test: Any matching logic that consumes ProfileVector data.

items.title: Show, decode, vouch - never prescribe
items.summary: The channel rule. Formats are structured so the mentor narrates their own path and decodes the terrain; prescription is out of scope.
items.violation_test: Session formats that ask mentors 'what should this student do?'; unscripted open advice formats for minors.

items.title: Family-visible by default
items.summary: Family-visible mentorship is both what parents expect and the safeguarding-correct default.
items.violation_test: Any early-phase format a parent cannot observe or review.

items.title: Curation, not marketplace
items.summary: Mentors are recruited, vetted, trained and few. One flaky or predatory mentor costs more than fifty good ones earn.
items.violation_test: Open sign-up flows; mentor counts as a vanity metric.

items.title: Observable formats only, for minors
items.summary: No private adult-minor channels in any early phase; all interaction happens in logged, observable formats.
items.violation_test: Any DM-like capability shipping before the T-6 preconditions are met.

items.title: Mentorship compounds into content
items.summary: Every mentor interaction should leave a permanent artifact that feeds the M1 content moat.
items.violation_test: Live formats with no capture-and-promote pipeline behind them.

items.title: Mentor-as-content
items.summary: Anyone filmed for a 'bir kun' video. Proof function at zero marginal cost; filming is the onboarding ritual.

items.title: Near-peers (workhorse tier)
items.summary: University students 3-6 years older from the same region: relatable proof plus decoding at scale, and lower safeguarding risk.

items.title: Professionals
items.summary: Working adults across pathways. Time-poor, so deploy in one-to-many formats rather than 1:1.

items.title: Ustalar
items.summary: Vocational masters. Must be recruited deliberately - vocational dignity parity fails by default otherwise.

items.title: Diaspora professionals
items.summary: Uzbeks abroad: decoding for study and work-abroad routes, async-friendly. Migration-adjacent content follows the E-9 surface rule.

items.title: Mentor as content
items.summary: Filmed 'bir kun' profiles; interview overflow becomes a pre-loaded Q&A bank under each card. No safeguarding surface because there is no interaction.

items.title: Async public Q&A under career cards
items.summary: Students ask under a card, vetted mentors answer, everything public and moderated before publication. Best answers are promoted into permanent card content.

items.title: School group sessions
items.summary: One mentor, one class or interest group, hosted and scheduled through the school advisor. One mentor-hour serves 25+ students.

items.title: Path cohorts
items.summary: Six to ten students on the same pathway, one mentor, four semi-scripted sessions. The script is the channel-rule enforcement mechanism.

items.title: Family consultations
items.summary: The mentor joins the family's congruence conversation as the credible third voice - broker provisioning, operationalized.

items.title: True 1:1
items.summary: Only much later, for older students: vetted, logged, gender-matched, parent-consented, and only by an explicit Decisions Log entry.

items.title: No private adult-minor channels
items.summary: No DM-like capability exists before T-6, which itself requires preconditions plus an explicit Decisions Log entry.
items.violation_test: Any direct-message capability between a mentor and a minor.

items.title: Observable and logged
items.summary: Every live format is recorded or minuted, parent-visible by default, and auditable.
items.violation_test: A live session with no record and no parent visibility.

items.title: Channel rule enforced structurally
items.summary: Formats are scripted or moderated such that prescription has no slot; violations are a removal offense.
items.violation_test: An unscripted, unmoderated advice format reaching minors.

items.title: No solicitation, no off-platform contact, no side payments
items.summary: Mentors may not sell to platform families, take contact details, or accept payment outside the platform. Signed at entry.
items.violation_test: Any surface that exposes contact details, or an unmoderated channel where solicitation can occur.

items.title: Vetting before live contact
items.summary: The vetting pipeline is mandatory and async probation precedes any live format.
items.violation_test: A mentor reaching a live format without a completed probation record.

items.title: Gender-matching for live proximity formats
items.summary: A parent-selectable default for T-4/T-5/T-6. A family consent choice about who is in the room - explicitly distinct from E-5, which forbids gender-conditional logic in scoring and matching.
items.violation_test: Gender-matching logic leaking into pathway or scoring code rather than staying in session composition.

items.title: Incident handling
items.summary: Zero-tolerance removal for safeguarding or solicitation violations; incident log reviewed by product leadership; schools notified where school-hosted.
items.violation_test: No reachable reporting mechanism for students, parents and advisors.

items.title: Minimal data exposure
items.summary: Mentors operate on pathway interest and context, never on profiles.
items.violation_test: Any mentor-reachable response containing ProfileVector or item-level data.

items.title: Volunteer/paid clarity
items.summary: Each tier's compensation status is explicit and public to mentors; ambiguity breeds the solicitation behavior ME-4 bans.
items.violation_test: A recruited tier with no stated compensation status.
